paragraphs.text: Some locations in this account are approximate.
Songtsän Gampo, a Tibetan emperor, was born here in 604 CE.
Lhasa, today the capital of Tibet, was founded in 633 CE.
The Potala Palace dates to 637 CE, and Songtsän Gampo moved the capital to it.

In 1240 the Mongol general Doorda Darkhan invaded Tibet with 30,000 troops, and in the late 1240s Mongol prince Godan invited Sakya Pandita, who urged other leading Tibetan figures to submit to Mongol authority.
Sonam Gyatso, born here in 1543 CE, was later named Dalai Lama by Altan Khan in 1578 for teachings in Mongolia.
Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, the 5th Dalai Lama, was born here in 1617 CE.
The wars of the Dzungar Khanate against the Qing dynasty, from 1688 CE to 1759 CE, reached Tibet.
In 1720 a Qing expedition took Tibet from the Dzungar Khanate and established Qing rule.
The Lhasa riot of 1750 began after two ambans assassinated Gyurme Namgyal, the expected new regent, and 51 Qing soldiers and 77 Chinese citizens were killed.
In 1788 a dispute over debased silver currency led to a Nepalese invasion of Tibet, followed by the Treaty of Kerung (1789).
Tibet fought the Kingdom of Jammu from May 1841 to August 1842.
The Nepalese-Tibetan War of 1855 to 1856 was fought in Tibet and ended with the Treaty of Thapathali.
In 1910 Qing China sent 2,000 troops to Tibet, causing the Dalai Lama to flee to British India.
